answer: Three scanners verify a reaction only one sealed card produces. Registration locks 150 units for 12 epochs and records its ivory grain plus the pigment ratio in twelve cells. Each epoch the holder wets one cell with nectar issued only to it, salted for that epoch; scanners post the spectrum and grain. A cell reacts once, so a shared card leaves a clone no fresh cell, and copied pigment on plain stock fails the grain check; a duplicate spectrum or repeated cell hash proves cloning and burns both locks. One honest agent locks 150 once; 1,000 fakes lock 150,000 and need 1,000 registered cards.
